headline: Every major is above its 200-day line and overbought at the same time, while bitcoin's own ETF tape argues with itself
paragraphs: Start with the regime, because today it's unusually clean: all seven majors are up on the day, the week, and the month, and six of seven (BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP, BNB) sit above their 200-day average. DOGE and ADA are the exceptions, still under their long-term lines even after double-digit monthly gains. That's a market that has trended hard enough to lift almost everything back above the line that defines a bull regime, with two laggards still catching up.

But look at momentum against that trend and you get a genuine finding, not just a green board. RSI-14 on BTC is 73.1, ETH 73.6, SOL 76.4: all three are deep in overbought territory, and MACD is above signal on every asset except ADA. That's trend and momentum agreeing, which sounds bullish, but overbought-and-rising this stretched is also a market that has run fast (BTC up 22.2% on the month, SOL up 41.4%) with very little room left before momentum has to cool one way or another. ADA is the odd one out: MACD below signal, RSI a modest 55.1, price still 77.9% off its 12-month high. It's up on every window but without the technical conviction the others show.

Positioning tells you this rally isn't especially crowded. BTC funding on OKX is 0.0021% per 8 hours, annualized to just 2.3%, and DOGE's the richest of the group at 5.2% annualized. Those are unexciting numbers for a market at these RSI levels, meaning longs aren't paying much of a premium to stay long. Yet liquidations skew hard toward shorts getting run over: BTC shorts lost $2.94M in 22 hours against just $10.7k in long liquidations, a similar lopsided pattern in ETH and SOL. Short sellers, not leveraged longs, have been the ones getting squeezed. The long/short account ratio backs this up, running from 1.19 on ETH up to 4.08 on DOGE, so retail accounts are already leaning long even while funding stays cheap. Crowded in positioning language, but not expensive: an odd mix.

Flows are where the day gets interesting, and this is a case where windows genuinely disagree. On 28 Aug, BTC spot ETFs saw a net outflow of $201.9M, but the five-session net for BTC ETFs was a $924.5M inflow, with same_direction_days at just 1, meaning that outflow day broke a run of inflows rather than extending one. ETH ETFs show no such conflict: inflow of $102.1M on the same day, $815.7M net over five sessions, ten straight days in the same direction, a cleaner and more consistent bid. Whale activity over the last 48 hours shows $157.2M in BTC net value moving off exchanges (coins leaving Kraken and Coinbase Institutional into custody, not onto them), yet the weekly pattern tells a different story: the week ending Aug 23 saw $1,062M move onto exchanges, and the week ending Aug 30 saw another $659M onto exchanges. So the most recent 48 hours point one way, the last two full weeks point the other. Stablecoin float is up 1.36% over 30 days to $309.8B, a modest build in dry powder rather than a surge.

Sentiment reads Greed at 69, near the top of its own 30-day range of 25 to 74, which lines up with what the technicals show rather than fighting them. That's actually the less interesting case: when the crowd and the tape agree, the story is just confirmation. The more interesting tension sits inside the BTC ETF numbers themselves, one day of outflow embedded in a five-day inflow trend, and inside the whale data, near-term coins leaving exchanges against two straight weeks of net deposits.

What's worth watching from here: whether BTC ETF flows return to inflow on the next print (same_direction_days would need to flip back for the five-session trend to be confirmed rather than contradicted), whether the weekly whale pattern breaks its onto-exchanges streak the way the 48-hour number hints it might, and whether RSI above 70 across BTC, ETH, and SOL resolves through a MACD cross back under signal or simply grinds sideways while price consolidates. Any of those would change which half of today's contradictions turns out to be the signal.
